First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{16}$ into the above, we get

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{16})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})
$$

which simplifies as

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16}).
$$

Therefore, we can simplify the given expression by rewriting the $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})$ in the numerator, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})} & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16})}} \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{16}).\end{aligned}
$$
